task.title: Repair the stale AWKIT-SEC-005 execution-service security assertion
task.objective: Repair the stale security verifier so AWKIT-SEC-005 proves the real validation-before-parse invariant at the authoritative execution-service layer (app/main/execution/ExecutionApplicationService.ts) instead of the vacated IPC module, prove the repaired assertion with two mutations that must both be rejected, and reconcile the authoritative defect and project-state records. Correct production security behavior must not be changed merely to turn the verifier green.

acceptance.description: AWKIT-SEC-005 inspects the authoritative readDataFile implementation in app/main/execution/ExecutionApplicationService.ts and proves, structurally and in order, that isReadableDataSourceFile runs before JSON.parse, AND that the parse consumes the same binding the guard validated; the assertion is not satisfied by the presence of either string alone, nor by correct ordering over an unvalidated path.

The authoritative defect record, known issues and project-state memory files record the verified SEC-005 outcome truthfully, the verifier registry stays consistent, and the derived roadmap dashboard still reports that sources agree.

61 passed, 0 failed (exit 0), including all 11 SEC-005 check lines. This is the measured post-Mutation-C count; the earlier 58/0 was an intermediate reading taken before the validated-binding clause and mutant C existed.

evidence.command: npm run verify:security (with readFile(resolved, ...) repointed to readFile(file, ...) inside the JSON.parse, leaving the guard and its ordering byte-identical)
evidence.observed: Predicate rejects mutant C, and a dedicated reason-specificity assertion proves it fails for the CONSUMPTION reason rather than incidental guard/order damage. Measured reason: 'parse does not consume the VALIDATED binding: the guard validated `resolved` but the parsed expression `JSON.parse(await readFile(file, "utf8"));` contains no `readFile(resolved, …)` — the parsed bytes come from a path the guard never checked'. Non-vacuity is asserted three ways: the surgery changed the text, the pre-parse prefix stayed byte-identical, and the mutant really names `file`. The reason-specificity assertion was itself mutation-tested (temporarily flipped to a sentinel prefix -> 60 passed, 1 failed; reverted -> 61 passed, 0 failed).

history.released_reason: SEC-005 verifier repair committed as bb99dfb with verify:security 61 passed 0 failed, build PASS, verifier-classification 5 of 5

completion.qa_basis: Granted on executed evidence, not on agent assertion. The repaired assertion was proven red-to-green against the real source: npm run verify:security measured 61 passed / 0 failed (exit 0), up from 52 passed / 1 failed before the repair; the intermediate 58/0 reading predates the validated-binding clause and mutant C and is superseded. All three security properties are proven structurally inside the authoritative readDataFile() body: the rejecting guard exists, it throws strictly before JSON.parse, and the parse consumes the same binding the guard validated (the identifier is derived from the guard's own third argument by a balanced-paren scan, so it cannot be satisfied by the token 'resolved' merely appearing somewhere). Each of the three mutants carries its own non-vacuity assertion, and mutant C additionally asserts the guard region is byte-identical and that rejection occurs for the consumption reason specifically rather than for incidental guard or order damage; the reason-specificity assertion was itself mutation-tested (60 passed / 1 failed when flipped to a sentinel, 61 passed / 0 failed when reverted). Supporting checks: npm run build PASS (tsc --noEmit clean), npm run verify:verifier-classification PASS (5/5, 200 classified / 202 files), git diff --check empty. Production source app/main/execution/ExecutionApplicationService.ts was NOT modified and is absent from git diff --stat, so no mutation artifact survived.
completion.qa_known_limitations: An independent GLM-5.3 read-only review raised one residual, adjudicated as non-blocking and inherent rather than as a defect in this changeset: sec005InvariantHolds is a textual predicate, so it proves the positive properties it asserts but cannot prove the ABSENCE of additional adversarial code in the body. A body that reassigned the validated binding after the guard, or that performed an extra unguarded read, could still satisfy it. Verified against source that the reassignment example would additionally require changing 'const resolved' (ExecutionApplicationService.ts:445) to 'let', so it does not typecheck as GLM stated it. GLM's second claim, that the anchor slice might span unrelated helper functions, was checked and does not hold in the current source: readDataFile ends at line 452 and resolveDataFilePath begins at line 454, so the extracted slice is exactly the function body. The residual risk of a future function being inserted between those two anchors is noted; the anchor guard asserts only bodyEnd > bodyStart. The predicate is strictly stronger than the assertion it replaced, which was fully vacuous.
